title: The Bronze Ox in the Summer Palace
synopsis: Have you seen the famous Bronze Ox at the Summer Palace? Why is his tail severed?

fullText.simplified:
颐和园铜牛的故事

    来中国的人一定会去北京，来北京的人一定会去颐和园。去了颐和园，一定能看到颐和园里的铜牛。关于颐和园的铜牛，我太爷爷给我讲过一个故事，今天我就把这个故事讲给大家听。
    相传，慈禧太后在建颐和园时，把自己想象成了天上的王母娘娘，所以打算把颐和园修成“天上人间”。佛香阁象征天宫，昆明湖就像是银河，八方亭和龙王庙等地方便是人间了。既然有银河，当然就要有牛郎和织女了。于是她命人在八方亭下面的昆明湖边上，放了一头铜牛，用来象征牛郎；在石舫的旁边又建了一座织女亭。铜牛的身子朝东，头朝西北，正对着织女亭的方向。
    有一年的农历七月初七，也就是天上的牛郎和织女见面的日子。这头铜牛突然活了。它离开了原来的位置，一步一步地走到湖里，朝着织女亭的方向游过去了。但是昆明湖实在是太大了，这头铜牛游到一半就沉到了湖底下，再也出不来了。
    铜牛不见了，慈禧马上又派人做了一只新的铜牛，放在了原来的地方。怕它还会跑，又用铁链子把它锁上了。
    到了第二年的农历七月初七，第二头铜牛又动了起来，眼看铁链子也锁不住了。慈禧赶忙让手下几个壮汉拉住铜牛。结果由于用力太大，“咔嚓”一声，把牛尾巴拉断了。
    这时候又有人找来了更粗的铁链子，费了九牛二虎之力总算把铜牛锁住了。从此昆明湖边上就留下了一只断了尾巴的铜牛。不过，这已经是第二只了。另一只呢？据说还在昆明湖底下呐！
    还没去过颐和园的朋友，有机会一定要去看看这头断了尾巴的铜牛。听说摸一摸还会有好运气呢！
fullText.traditional:
頤和園銅牛的故事

    來中國的人一定會去北京，來北京的人一定會去頤和園。去了頤和園，一定能看到頤和園裡的銅牛。關於頤和園的銅牛，我太爺爺給我講過一個故事，今天我就把這個故事講給大家聽。
    相傳，慈禧太后在建頤和園時，把自己想像成了天上的王母娘娘，所以打算把頤和園修成“天上人間”。佛香閣象徵天宮，昆明湖就像是銀河，八方亭和龍王廟等地方便是人間了。既然有銀河，當然就要有牛郎和織女了。於是她命人在八方亭下面的昆明湖邊上，放了一頭銅牛，用來象徵牛郎；在石舫的旁邊又建了一座織女亭。銅牛的身子朝東，頭朝西北，正對著織女亭的方向。
    有一年的農曆七月初七，也就是天上的牛郎和織女見面的日子。這頭銅牛突然活了。它離開了原來的位置，一步一步地走到湖裡，朝著織女亭的方向游過去了。但是昆明湖實在是太大了，這頭銅牛游到一半就沉到了湖底下，再也出不來了。
    銅牛不見了，慈禧馬上又派人做了一隻新的銅牛，放在了原來的地方。怕它還會跑，又用鐵鏈子把它鎖上了。
    到了第二年的農曆七月初七，第二頭銅牛又動了起來，眼看鐵鏈子也鎖不住了。慈禧趕忙讓手下幾個壯漢拉住銅牛。結果由於用力太大，“咔嚓”一聲，把牛尾巴拉斷了。
    這時候又有人找來了更粗的鐵鏈子，費了九牛二虎之力總算把銅牛鎖住了。從此昆明湖邊上就留下了一隻斷了尾巴的銅牛。不過，這已經是第二隻了。另一隻呢？據說還在昆明湖底下吶！
    還沒去過頤和園的朋友，有機會一定要去看看這頭斷了尾巴的銅牛。聽說摸一摸還會有好運氣呢！

sentences.english: .. and exerting tremendous strength finally managed to secure the Bronze Ox.

sentences.english: Since then, there has been a Bronze Ox with a broken tail at the edge of Kunming Lake.
But, this is the second ox. What about the first one? Legend has it that it’s still at the bottom of Kunming Lake!

sentences.pinyin: yǒu jī huì yí dìng yào qù kàn kan zhè tóu duàn le wěi ba de tóng niú
sentences.english: For folks who haven’t yet been to the Summer Palace, ..

sentences.simplified: 听说摸一摸还会有好运气呢！
sentences.traditional: 聽說摸一摸還會有好運氣呢！
sentences.pinyin: tīng shuō mō yì mō hái huì yǒu hǎo yùn qi ne
sentences.english: .. if you get the chance, you should make a visit to see the Bronze Ox with a severed tail.
It’s said that touching it even brings good fortune!

raw.synopsis: Have you seen the famous Bronze Ox at the Summer Palace? Why is his tail severed?
sentence_translations: The Story of the Bronze Ox at the Summer Palace
People who come to China will definitely visit Beijing, ..
.. and those who come to Beijing will definitely visit the Summer Palace.
When visiting the Summer Palace, you can definitely see the Bronze Ox at the Summer Palace.
My great grandfather once told me a story about the Bronze Ox at the Summer Palace.
Today, I’m going to tell this story to you all.
According to legend, when Empress Dowager Cixi had the Summer Palace built, ..
.. she imagined herself as Queen Mother of the West.
So, she planned to build the Summer Palace like a “heaven on earth”.
The Tower of Buddhist Incense represents a heavenly palace, and Kunming Lake represents the Milky Way.
Places such as the Kuoru Pavilion and the Temple of the Dragon King represent the human world.
Since there was a Milky Way, it goes without saying that there should also be a cowherd and a weaver girl.
So, she ordered a Bronze Ox to be placed under the Kuoru pavilion on the edge of Kunming Lake to represent the Cowherd.
Next to the Marble Boat, she built a Weaver Girl Pavilion.
The body of the Bronze Ox faced east and the head faced northwest, ..
.. directly in the direction of the Weaving Girl Pavilion.
One year during the Qixi Festival, the day when the cowherd and the weaver girl meet in the sky, ..
.. the Bronze Ox suddenly came alive.
It left its original location, walked step by step into the lake, ..
.. and swam out in the direction of the Weaver Girl Pavilion.
But the Kunming Lake was so big that after swimming halfway, the Bronze Ox sunk to the bottom of the lake, ..
.. never to come out again.
The Bronze Ox disappeared, so Cixi immediately sent someone to make a new one and place it in the original location.
Scared that it might run away too, she locked it up with an iron chain.
During the Qixi Festival the following year, the second Bronze Ox began moving once again.
Seeing the iron chain was about to break, Cixi hurriedly requested some burly men to hold the Bronze Ox in place.
They used too much force, and with a “snapping” sound, the ox’s tail was severed.
At this time, some people found a thicker iron chain, ..
.. and exerting tremendous strength finally managed to secure the Bronze Ox.
Since then, there has been a Bronze Ox with a broken tail at the edge of Kunming Lake.
But, this is the second ox. What about the first one? Legend has it that it’s still at the bottom of Kunming Lake!
For folks who haven’t yet been to the Summer Palace, ..
.. if you get the chance, you should make a visit to see the Bronze Ox with a severed tail.
It’s said that touching it even brings good fortune!
